messages.subject: DSM response variable
parts:
Hi everybody,

 

I’m running a density surface model with line transect data.

I have a couple of questions:


1-What happens if there are no observation in a segment when calculating the response variable? Seen the formulae to calculate density or abundance, I believe they will be just zeros, but I just wanted to be sure about it.


2- I wanted to look at the response variable and after running the DSM I called:

DSM_model$data. This returned the table with segment data with 3 more columns:

Density.est, off.set and area.segment.


So I guess the DSM will use the column density.est as the response variable.

I have 2487 segments, 633 observations in total, some segments (248 have more than one observation).

I don’t understand how is it possible that when I call DSM_model$data in the response variable in 70 segments only density is>0. 

I’ve also tried count and abundance.est just to see if it was the type of response variable specification causing weird behavior.  

I know that the response variable is calculated in different ways for density, count, and abundance but seen that they consistently show the same 70 segments I was wondering if I was looking for the response variable in the correct place? Is there any other way to see the response variable?


In another post, I've found that the response variable is in DSM_model$results$data. That didn’t work, as $results is not an object returned from the DSM.

If I’m looking in the correct place, is this kind of response variable plausible?

In the example with mexico-dolphins, the observations occur in 40 segments. When I call DSM_model$data, in the mexico example the response variable count is >0 in 40 of the segments, showing a more plausible calculation of the response variable. 


I can send my database to anyone willing to help. 


Thank you!


Valentina Zini

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM response variable
parts:
Valentina

All you say is correct; the <dsmobject>$data$count will hold the number of objects detected in each of your segments.  It should be a reflection of your sightings.  Segments without sightings should have zeroes.  Something is suspicious if you have only 70 non-zero values for <dsmobject>$data$count if you have sightings in other segments.  You'll need to re-check your data organisation.
